BAGONG PLIP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg,gov.ph OPINION NO MAY 22 LEOCADIO T. TROVELA, CESO Ill Regional Director DILG Region VII — Central Visayas Sudlon, Lahug Cebu City Dear RD Trovela: This refers to your letter dated 29 February 2024 in relation to the letter of Hon. Braulio Novicio Umandac, Punong Barangay, Amatugan, Tuburan, Cebu requesting for permission to be allowed to claim backwages from the date he was arrested for violation of Republic Act No. 10591 (illegal possession of firearms and ammunition) up to the time of his acquittal pursuant to the Decision dated 28 July 2022 of the Regional Trial Court Branch 29, Toledo City, Cebu. At the outset, the Central Office concurs with your position that barangay officials are not entitled to the payment of the monthly honorarium in the absence of the required actual services rendered by the claimant thereof. DILG Opinion No. 28, series of 2017, citing DILG Opinion No. 16, series of 2017, is instructive regarding the issue, viz: "It bears to note that under DBM Local Budget Circular No. 631, in relation to Section 393 of the Local Govemment Code, Sangguniang Barangay Members are paid in the form of honorarium. Corollary thereto, the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual defines honorarium as the remuneration given to a public official for services actually rendered. Hence the grant of honorarium is based principally on services actually rendered by the claimant thereof. Accordingly, other than certain factors, the most convenient way of measuring the services actually rendered by a Sangguniang Barangay Member is attendance in sessions. Under the Local Government Code, Sangguniang Barangays are mandated to conduct two sessions a month. The honorarium can, therefore, be divided into two pads, each representing each session. Hence, if a Sangguniang Barangay Member will absent himself from sessions, he is not entitled to receive the proportionate amount of honorarium for services actually rendered. If he will be absent in both sessions for one month, then he can be deprived of his total honorarium for that month" 1 Entitled: POSITION CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND PERSONNEL "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

Further, by definition under the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM), honorarium is a remuneration given to a public official for services actually rendered, to be entitled to an honorarium. In view of the foregoing, considering that Hon. Braulio Novicio Umandac, Punong Barangay, Amatugan, Tuburan, Cebu has been arrested for violation of Republic Act No. 10591 (illegal possession of firearms and ammunition) up to the time of his acquittal pursuant to the Decision dated 28 July 2022 of the Regional Trial Court Branch 29, Toledo City, Cebu, he was not able to render actual service. Hence, he is not entitled to the payment of monthly honorarium. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you Very truly yours, BY T AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . JUAN VICTOR R.
